content.intro: This lesson introduces Monitoring and Error Reporting using the supplied syllabus terms, a visual map, and a short inspectable example.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding Monitoring and Error Reporting helps you make JavaScript behavior explicit instead of relying on guesswork. The skill becomes more valuable as programs combine data, user input, runtime APIs, and failures.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Monitoring and Error Reporting is one of the named concepts in the JavaScript syllabus. Focus on the behavior it defines, the inputs that influence that behavior, and the result you can observe. JavaScript language semantics are specified by ECMAScript; browser and Node.js APIs belong to their host runtimes, so check which environment a feature requires.

content_blocks.title: Build the idea in small steps

items.title: Runtime error collection
items.text: Use Runtime error collection to observe the program rather than guess: reproduce one case, inspect the relevant value or stack trace, change one thing, then verify the fix.

items.title: Performance metrics
items.text: For Performance metrics, start with a correct baseline and representative input. Measure before and after any optimization; avoid trading away clarity for an unverified speed improvement.

items.title: Structured server logs
items.text: Practise Structured server logs with the smallest example that demonstrates the syntax, then change one input to see which part of the result changes.

items.title: Avoiding sensitive data in telemetry
items.text: Connect Avoiding sensitive data in telemetry to Monitoring and Error Reporting. Define the expected behavior first, demonstrate it with a small example, and explain one edge case before using it in a larger program.

content_blocks.run_instructions: This example is an inspectable teaching snippet, not an arbitrary-code execution service inside CodeLeaf. Save it as a small .js file and run it with a supported Node.js release for console-only examples, or place browser-only code in an HTML page with the required element. Compare the actual output with the expectation and change one input at a time.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the initial snippet, remove temporary logging, and repeat with one boundary or invalid input.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: First, name the expected result for Monitoring and Error Reporting. Then trace the code one statement at a time: record the important value before and after each operation, and check whether the output matches your expectation. Change one input or condition; if the result is different, inspect that step instead of rewriting the whole program.

content_blocks.title: Environment and correctness note
content_blocks.text: The ECMAScript 2026 edition is the stable language reference used by this course. The browser DOM, Fetch API, and Node.js APIs are host features. Emerging proposals and runtime support can change; verify compatibility before depending on a feature in production.

content.task: Try it yourself: create a small program that demonstrates Monitoring and Error Reporting. Use at least one of the listed subtopics (Runtime error collection), include one normal input and one edge case, and write two sentences explaining why the observed result makes sense.
task_acceptance_criteria: The program uses the lesson concept accurately and has readable names.
The learner states the expected result and checks the actual result.
At least one edge case, failure path, or environment assumption is addressed.
hints: Reduce the program to the smallest example that still shows the concept.
Trace values and control flow from the first statement to the output.
Use the linked official reference when behavior is unclear.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a snippet without understanding its input and output.
common_mistakes.why: A memorized example can appear to work while hiding assumptions about input values or runtime.
common_mistakes.fix: Explain the expected output first, run the smallest example, and test one boundary case.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming browser APIs are part of core JavaScript.
common_mistakes.why: ECMAScript does not define the browser DOM or Node.js filesystem APIs.
common_mistakes.fix: Identify the host environment and consult its official API reference.

common_mistakes.why: Several simultaneous edits make the cause of a behavior difficult to isolate.
common_mistakes.fix: Change one variable or line, reproduce the result, and record what changed.
